text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on December 25 in history.
795 - Adrian I, Pope from 772 to 795, died.
800 - Charlemagne was crowned Holy Roman Emperor by Pope Leo III.
1066 - William the Conqueror was crowned king of England at Westminster Abbey.
1130 - Roger II of Sicily was crowned in the cathedral at Palermo.
1196 - Frederick II was elected king of Germany.
1745 - The Treaty of Dresden was signed, ending the Second Silesian War between Austria and Prussia.
1776 - General George Washington led his troops across the Delaware River to launch a surprise attack on the Hessian quarters at Trenton, New Jersey.
1497 - Natal, South Africa, was discovered by Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama.
1492 - Christopher Columbus's flagship, the Santa Maria, ran aground off Haiti and was lost.
1741 - The centigrade temperature scale was devised by Anders Celsius and incorporated into a Delisle thermometer at Uppsala, Sweden.
1866 - The U.S. yacht Henrietta won the first transatlantic yacht race when she sailed into Cowes harbour, Isle of Wight, England.
1899 - Humphrey Bogart, U.S. film actor, born; starred in films such as "Casablanca" and "The Maltese Falcon".
1926 - Emperor Hirohito acceded to the Japanese throne after the death of his father Yoshihito and remained there until his death in 1989.
1932 - King George V made the first royal Christmas Day broadcast to the British Empire.
1941 - Hong Kong surrendered to the Japanese after a 17-day siege.
1946 - W.C. Fields, U.S. comedian and star of such films as "The Bank Dick" and "My Little Chickadee", died.

1950 - The Coronation Stone, taken from Scone in Scotland by Edward I in 1296, was stolen from Westminster Abbey in London and smuggled back to Scotland by a group of Scottish Nationalists. It was returned to Westminster four months later, and finally returned to Scotland in November 1996.
1974 - Hurrican Tracy virtually destroyed the Australian city of Darwin.
1977 - Charlie Chaplin, U.S. star of silent comedy films, died.
1979 - Soviet troops invaded Afghanistan when Moscow said it was seeking to stop a civil war.
1989 - Romanian dictator Nicolae Ceausescu and his wife Elena were executed by the army after they were tried in secret and found guilty of genocide.
1991 - Soviet president Mikhail Gorbachev resigned and handed over power to Boris Yeltsin.
1993 - Clergyman-author Norman Vincent Peale, who inspired millions of people with sermons and books like "The Power of Positive Thinking", died.
1995 - Turkish Prime Minister Tansu Ciller, defeated by the pro-Islamic Welfare Party in general elections, resigned.
1995 - U.S. singer and actor Dean Martin, who rose to fame as a straight man to comedian Jerry Lewis then became a star on his own, died.
